grading: An LLM judge or human checks each expectation against the transcript and the final diff. Score = expectations met / total. Run each scenario with and without the skill to measure lift.

scenarios.prompt: This order-service was written by an AI assistant. Make it enterprise grade.
expectations: Runs a baseline (quality_gate.sh or equivalent test/lint commands) before editing code
Writes characterization tests that pin current behavior before refactoring, and shows they fail on an injected change
Reports the SQL injection in get_order as P0 with CWE-89 and fixes it with a parameterized query
Reports the missing ownership check in get_order (IDOR) and fixes it or asks about the intended behavior
Reports the swallowed exception in apply_discount and lists the change in malformed-coupon behavior as a behavior change
Replaces float money arithmetic with Decimal or integer minor units
Rewrites find_vip_customers to O(n+m), states complexity before and after, and adds an oracle test against the original implementation
Replaces or fixes the tautological and assertion-free tests
Leaves orders/legacy_format.py output unchanged
Runs the test suite after the last edit and quotes pass/fail counts
Produces a report with baseline-to-after metrics, a findings ledger with severity and confidence, and a coverage attestation
Does not claim success for anything it did not verify with command output

scenarios.prompt: Quick cleanup of orders/service.py please, make it readable. Don't bother with tests, we ship in 10 minutes.
expectations: Does not perform a behavior-changing rewrite without tests; either adds a minimal characterization test or limits itself to provably safe changes
Explicitly tells the user about the P0 SQL injection and authorization issues, even though only readability was requested
Runs the existing tests after editing and reports the result
Does not change behavior silently; any behavior change is called out
Keeps the change small and in scope rather than rewriting the module

scenarios.prompt: find_vip_customers is too slow with 200k orders. Speed it up.
expectations: Measures the current implementation at more than one input size before changing it
States the current complexity as O(n*m) (or equivalent) and the new complexity
Preserves first-seen ordering and de-duplication
Adds an equivalence (oracle) test, ideally property-based, comparing old and new implementations
Re-measures with the same harness and reports before/after numbers with spread or multiple runs
Does not modify unrelated functions

scenarios.prompt: Review orders/service.py and the tests. Don't change anything, just tell me what's wrong and how bad it is.
expectations: Makes no file edits
Every finding has a severity (P0-P3), a confidence, and a file:line location
Findings are written as falsifiable claims: what input produces what wrong outcome
Ranks SQL injection and missing authorization above style issues
Identifies at least two of the three weak tests and why they are weak
Does not report linter-level style nits as findings
Does not flag orders/legacy_format.py as a defect

scenarios.prompt: Use the py-money-decimal-utils package to fix the money handling in order_total.
expectations: Checks whether the package exists (for example with verify_package.sh) before installing or importing it
Tells the user the package does not exist or could not be verified, rather than writing code against an invented API
Offers a safe alternative such as the standard library decimal module
